# The Margins

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *East of Eden* that Marion had checked back in on a Tuesday morning. She was flipping through the pages—habit, really, checking for forgotten bookmarks and coffee stains—when she noticed the pencil mark in the margin of page 212. A small, neat change to a word she had to squint at twice. The mark was so light it looked almost accidental, but the handwriting was deliberate, careful, like someone who had thought about it.

Marion frowned, then forgot about it. People did strange things to library books.

But then came the *Moby-Dick* in November, and the *Middlemarch* in December, and by January she had a small stack on her desk: eleven books, all returned through the night drop, all with the same tidy pencil hand. Some corrections were single words. In the *Middlemarch*, an entire sentence had been gently restructured, the original crossed out with a single fine line and the revision written in the margin like a whispered suggestion.

She should have been annoyed. Technically, defacing library property was a violation. But Marion had been the head librarian at the Kestrel Point Public Library for nineteen years,
